title: The breath that won: prana
hookLine: the senses argue over which of them matters most, and the breath settles it by leaving
carry: prana: the breath is life, and sacred
tomorrow: why do Hindu chants end with peace three times?

lines: SPEECH, EYE, EAR, MIND: WHO IS GREATEST?
cards: The Chandogya Upanishad tells of a quarrel inside a person. Speech, the eye, the ear and the mind each claim to be the greatest, so they go to their father, Prajapati, the Creator, to judge.
He says: the greatest is the one whose leaving leaves the body worst off. Speech leaves for a year. The body lives on, mute.
The eye leaves; it lives on, blind. The ear goes, then the mind; still it lives. Then the breath begins to go, and it tears all the others loose, like a strong horse pulling up its tethering pegs.

teach.h: STAY. YOU ARE THE BEST OF US.
teach.b: They all cry out: stay. You are the best of us. That breath is prana, and this little story is one of the Upanishads' ways of saying that breath isn't just air.
Prana is the life in you, the power that keeps speech and sight and thought alive. Hindu practice takes that seriously.

teach.h: BREATH FIRST, THEN THE SACRED WORDS.
teach.b: The daily prayer called sandhya includes pranayama near its start: the breath is steadied before the sacred words are said.
Later in the same Upanishad, the first bites of a meal are offered to the breath within, with the words prāṇāya svāhā, to prana, I offer; some traditional families still begin meals that way.
And the alphabet itself remembers. Sanskrit grammarians sort consonants by breath.

teach.h: ALPAPRANA, MAHAPRANA: LITTLE BREATH, GREAT BREATH.
teach.b: A plain consonant is alpaprana, little breath. One written with an h is mahaprana, great breath.
That h isn't a new sound. It's a puff of air. So bh is a b that breathes, as in clubhouse: Bhagavan, the Lord, and bhakti, devotion, both open with it.

Dh is a d that breathes, as in roadhouse: dharma lets out a little air before it says anything else. Even atha, now, the first word of the Yoga Sutras, is a t at the teeth and then breath, never the th of thin.

teach.h: EVERY HOLY WORD RIDES ON PRANA.
teach.b: Many teachers put it simply: every holy word rides out on prana. To say a name of God with its breath let through is to offer the very thing the whole body, in the story, couldn't live without.

how: Many Hindus begin daily prayer (sandhya) with pranayama, steadying the breath before the mantras; some traditional families offer the first bites of a meal to prana with prāṇāya svāhā; Sanskrit students learn each consonant plain and breathed, sometimes with a hand before the mouth to feel the breath.

o: a b said with the tongue curled back
a b with great breath, as in Bhagavan and bhakti
a b and h blended like the v in very

games.q: the breath that won — tap the pairs.
p: leaves for a year; the body lives on, mute
the breath, which the others cannot live without
great breath: a consonant with an h
the first bite of a meal, offered to the breath

s: in the Chandogya story, the mind wins the contest of the senses
the breath wins: when it starts to leave, it pulls all the others with it.
the daily prayer called sandhya includes pranayama, steadying the breath
the breath is steadied before the sacred words are said.
the th in atha is said like the th in thin
it's a t at the teeth, then breath: great breath, mahaprana.

games.q: the senses ask Prajapati which of them is greatest. what test does he give them?
o: see which one speaks the loudest.
see whose leaving leaves the body worst off.
games.why: each leaves for a year, and the body gets by. when the breath starts to go, everything goes with it: prana is the life in you.

practice: Sit the way many begin sandhya: back easy, a few slow breaths, just noticing prana come and go. Then hold your palm near your mouth and say ba, then bha; da, then dha, feeling the great breath land on your hand.
If you pray, say one name you pray with, Bhagavan or another, letting every breath letter breathe, as an offering. If not, say dharma slowly and feel the air move.

wordCard.voice: Bha. A b with great breath, the sound that opens Bhagavan and bhakti: prana, riding out inside a letter.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: bha, b with breath, the first sound of Bhagavan. A mahaprana, great-breath letter.

carryVoice: Your line: prana: the breath is life, and sacred. Every holy word rides out on it. Rest well.
